subject.title: fix: Node allowlist writeback can restore revoked exec approvals

question: Should this conflicting external branch be repaired/rebased as the security-boundary fix for stale node exec approval writeback, or should maintainers replace it with a narrower current-main branch?
rationale: The central issue is valid and security-sensitive, but the proposed branch changes exec approval persistence, conflicts with main, and still has incomplete guarded-write coverage, so adoption versus replacement needs maintainer ownership.

options.title: Repair and rebase this PR
options.body: Refresh the branch onto current main, preserve current exec approval persistence behavior, close the unguarded initialization write, update CLI tests, and require real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Replace with a narrower maintainer branch
options.body: Use this PR as design input but land a smaller current-main fix if conflict resolution would replace most of the branch.

options.title: Pause until contributor proof and rebase arrive
options.body: Keep the PR open but out of merge paths until the contributor supplies real behavior proof and a clean branch.

recommendation.title: Repair and rebase this PR
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch onto current main, preserve current exec approval persistence behavior, close the unguarded initialization write, update CLI tests, and require real behavior proof before merge.
